name: ATIC
summary: Historical Antarctic balloon cosmic-ray calorimeter. Electron-spectrum structure prompted discussion of dark matter and nearby cosmic-ray sources, forming important historical context for indirect searches.
detection_principle: Calorimetry and charge measurements reconstruct cosmic-ray electron and nuclear spectra, using high-energy electron excesses to test source models.

status.label: Data taking ended / historical experiment
status.evidence: LSU's 2015 material reviews ATIC balloon missions as preceding work for CALET.

key_parameters.name: Historical excess interval
key_parameters.value: 300–800 GeV, reported in 2008; not a measurement of dark-matter mass

results.summary: Electron-spectrum anomalies may be discussed in terms of unidentified astrophysical sources or dark-matter scenarios; they cannot be recorded as dark-matter discoveries.

science_scope: Tests dark-matter models through astrophysical radiation, cosmic rays or neutrinos. Astrophysical backgrounds and propagation models affect interpretation; an anomaly alone does not establish dark matter.
